title: N-Queens
statement:
Count the ways to place `n` queens on an `n` by `n` chessboard so that no two queens attack each other. A queen attacks every square in its row, in its column, and along both of its diagonals.

The input is one whole number `n`, from 1 to 9. Print the number of ways to place the `n` queens. Two placements are different when some square holds a queen in one of them and not in the other, so mirror images and rotations of a placement all count.

For `n = 4` there are two ways. Listing the queens' columns from the top row down, counting from 1, they are `2 4 1 3` and `3 1 4 2`.

Input:

```text
4
```

Expected output:

```text
2
```
hints: Every row holds exactly one queen, so place them one row at a time. In the current row, try each column where a new queen would be safe, then go on to the next row. Getting past the last row means you've found one placement.

Keep track of the columns and the diagonals that already hold a queen. The squares on one diagonal going down to the right all share `row - col`, and the squares on one diagonal going down to the left all share `row + col`.

Mark the column and both diagonals before you recurse and clear them after, so the next column you try starts from the same board. Sets work, and so do arrays of true and false values, where `row - col + n - 1` turns the first diagonal into an index from 0.

python.solution:
def count_n_queens(n: int) -> int:
    cols: set[int] = set()
    down_diagonals: set[int] = set()  # by row - col
    up_diagonals: set[int] = set()  # by row + col

    # Places a queen in this row and in every row below it.
    def place(row: int) -> int:
        if row == n:
            return 1
        count = 0
        for col in range(n):
            if col in cols or row - col in down_diagonals or row + col in up_diagonals:
                continue
            cols.add(col)
            down_diagonals.add(row - col)
            up_diagonals.add(row + col)
            count += place(row + 1)
            cols.remove(col)
            down_diagonals.remove(row - col)
            up_diagonals.remove(row + col)
        return count

    return place(0)


n = int(input())
print(count_n_queens(n))
